did_you_know.text: Did you know? The prophecy identifies Bethlehem Ephrathah as a relatively small place among the clans of Judah, yet from it a ruler over Israel will come. It also says that his origins are very ancient—“from ancient times, from the days of eternity.”

Did you know? According to the verse, the period of waiting for the ruler’s appearance continues until “the time when she who is in labor gives birth.” After that, “the rest of his brothers” will return to the people of Israel.
Did you know? The future ruler is described as a shepherd: he will stand and shepherd his flock “in the strength of the LORD,” and his rule will extend “to the ends of the earth.”
Did you know? Alongside the promise of peace, the verse describes the possibility of a threat from Assyria. In that case, “seven shepherds and eight human leaders” will be raised up against it.

Did you know? The role of the shepherds and leaders is not only to defend Israel: they are described as shepherding the land of Assyria and the land of Nimrod with the sword, thereby saving Israel from an Assyrian invasion.

Did you know? The remnant of Jacob is compared to dew and showers on the grass—phenomena that do not depend on a person’s request or expectation. The image emphasizes the remnant’s presence and influence among many peoples.

Did you know? The remnant is also described using a contrasting and less gentle image: as a lion and a young lion among the beasts of the forest and flocks of sheep, symbolizing a strength that no one can withstand.
Did you know? “On that day” the LORD will remove Israel’s war horses and chariots—things associated with military power—as part of the transformation of circumstances described in the chapter.
Did you know? The chapter also includes the elimination of magical forces and beliefs: the LORD promises to remove sorceries from Israel and prevent the existence of soothsayers.

Did you know? Alongside the removal of sorceries and soothsayers, the LORD promises to remove the idols and sacred pillars, so that the people will no longer bow down to what their own hands have made.
